claims.text: Real-time adaptive laser-power modulation during selective laser melting stabilizes melt-pool dynamics.
Stabilizing the melt pool through adaptive laser-power modulation improves dimensional precision.
Adaptive laser-power modulation enhances mechanical integrity by reducing fabrication-induced defects.
High-entropy-alloy components made by fixed-power SLM exhibit inconsistent melt-pool dynamics.
High-entropy-alloy components made by fixed-power SLM exhibit porosity and dimensional inaccuracies.
Real-time melt-pool monitoring can enable dynamic adjustment of laser power during layer-by-layer fabrication.
Stabilized melt-pool dynamics produce more uniform thermal gradients and controlled solidification.
More stable melt-pool dynamics produce a refined, homogeneous microstructure.
Modulating laser power in response to real-time melt-pool measurements counteracts fluctuations in energy input.
Counteracting fluctuations in energy input minimizes localized overheating and underheating.
Melt-pool stabilization prevents porosity and microcrack formation.
Reduced residual stress, porosity, and microcracking improve dimensional fidelity and mechanical strength.
Relative to fixed-power SLM, adaptive modulation will yield statistically significant improvement in dimensional accuracy.
Relative to fixed-power SLM, adaptive modulation will increase tensile strength.
Relative to fixed-power SLM, adaptive modulation will reduce porosity and the number of microcracks.
Insufficient sensor resolution or response time may limit the benefits of adaptive laser-power modulation.
The effect of adaptive modulation may depend on alloy composition and machine constraints.
